title: Egg Omelet or Scrambled Egg with Meat

content.title: About
content.content: Egg omelet or scrambled egg with meat is a dish made from beaten eggs mixed with a splash of milk or cream and cooked on a skillet together with pieces of cooked or fried meat (ham, bacon, chicken). The “NS” label refers to the fat type used in preparation, according to the 1992 classification.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs are a complete source of protein, containing all essential amino acids.
Adding meat boosts iron and vitamin B12 content.
The “NS” (non‑standard) fat type denotes the use of fats high in saturated fatty acids.
Omelets can be prepared French‑style (soft, slightly runny) or Russian‑style (firm, fully set).
Traditionally the dish is served with herbs, tomatoes, or bread.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Eggs and meat together provide a high level of biologically available protein, supporting tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish contains vitamins B2, B6 and B12, important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Meat adds heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Supports eye health
items.content: Egg yolk is rich in lutein and zeaxanthin, antioxidants that protect the eyes.

items.title: Provides sustained energy
items.content: The combination of fats and proteins offers lasting satiety and stable energy levels.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: The NS fat type may raise LDL‑cholesterol when consumed frequently.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to eggs, experiencing reactions from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Egg yolks contain cholesterol; people with elevated cholesterol should limit intake.

items.title: Salt and processed meat
items.content: Sausages and bacon often contain high levels of salt and nitrates, which may be undesirable for hypertension.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Beat eggs with a small amount of milk, season with salt and pepper. In a heated skillet with a little NS‑type fat, sauté diced meat, then pour in the egg mixture. Cook, stirring, until desired consistency is reached. Optionally add herbs, cheese, or vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best enjoyed fresh. If needed, store in the refrigerator in an airtight container for up to 24 hours. Reheat in a skillet or microwave, adding a bit of oil to prevent drying out.
